description: The relations family fed by live LogQL against lgtm-loki. A metric query returns the same frame shape Prometheus does — one frame per series, endpoints in labels — so the same two routes apply: a ranged query with an empty Transform tab, and an instant query reshaped with organize + rowsToFields for per-edge ids. The flows are where the stack's own log lines come from: which service, which logger, which level.

options.content:
# Relations charts from Loki logs

The relations panel needs one field for each edge. Each edge must identify its source and target.

These examples use the following Loki values:

| Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `service_name` | Identifies the service that wrote the log line. |
| `detected_level` | Identifies the log level that Loki detected. |
| `logger` | Identifies the Grafana logger after `| logfmt` parses the line. |
| `job="lgtm/docker"` | Selects the container log streams for this stack. |

`detected_level` is structured metadata. Grafana must add this filter after the stream selector. These queries end with `logfmt` so Grafana puts ad hoc filters in the pipeline. This is a workaround for [a Grafana Loki data source issue](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-loki-datasource/issues/155).

## Route A: ranged series

A ranged LogQL metric query returns one `Value` field for each series. Use `label_format` to add `source` and `target` labels to that field.

Keep the original endpoint labels in the outer aggregation. The panel uses their matching values to detect the filter names.

The panel reads each labeled field as an edge. This route does not need a transformation.

## Route B: instant rows

An instant query returns one row for each series. Use `label_format` to create a unique `edge` label.

Use Organize fields to put `edge` first and rename the endpoint columns to `source` and `target`. Keep the original endpoint columns. Then use Rows to fields.

This route creates a named field for each edge. You can use the field name in an override.

Each relations panel enables ad hoc filters. Pin a tooltip to add a filter to the Ad hoc filters variable.

panels.title: Route A — service → level, no transformations
panels.description:
This Sankey chart groups log lines by service and detected level. The ranged query adds `source` and `target` labels with `label_format`.

The outer aggregation keeps `service_name` and `detected_level`. The panel uses these original labels for ad hoc filters.

The Transform tab is empty because the panel reads the labels directly. The Sum calculation adds the counts from all time buckets.

Node values are off because the query supplies edge values only. A derived node has no service total.

panels.title: Route B — service → logger, with per-edge ids
panels.description:
This graph uses an instant query and creates an `edge` label in LogQL. Organize fields puts `edge` first and renames `src` and `dst` to `source` and `target`.

The query and transformation keep `service_name` and `logger`. The panel uses these original endpoint labels for ad hoc filters.

Rows to fields creates one named field for each edge. The `grafana-->migrator` override changes only that edge.

targets.expr:
topk(12,
  sum by (edge, src, dst, service_name, logger) (
    count_over_time(
      {job="lgtm/docker"} | logfmt
        | label_format src=`{{.service_name}}`, dst=`{{.logger}}`
        | dst != ""
        | label_format edge=`{{.src}}-->{{.dst}}`
      [$__range]
    )
  )
)

panels.title: Three tiers from two queries — grafana → logger → level
panels.description:
This Sankey chart combines two ranged queries. Query A supplies `service → logger` edges, and query B supplies `logger → level` edges.

Both queries keep their original endpoint labels after they add `source` and `target`. The panel detects the correct ad hoc filter names for each edge.

The logger allow-list keeps the middle column stable across the selected time range. Some logger lines have no detected level, so the totals can differ.

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target, service_name, logger) (
  count_over_time(
    {job="lgtm/docker", service_name="grafana"} | logfmt
      | logger =~ `migrator|authn.service|resource-migrator|tsdb.loki|context|backgroundsvcs.managerAdapter`
      | label_format source=`{{.service_name}}`, target=`{{.logger}}`
      | target != ""
    [$__auto]
  )
)

sum by (source, target, logger, detected_level) (
  count_over_time(
    {job="lgtm/docker", service_name="grafana"} | logfmt
      | logger =~ `migrator|authn.service|resource-migrator|tsdb.loki|context|backgroundsvcs.managerAdapter`
      | label_format source=`{{.logger}}`, target=`{{.detected_level}}`
      | target != ""
    [$__auto]
  )
)

panels.title: Service × level as a matrix — chord
panels.description:
This chord chart uses the same service-to-level query as the Sankey chart. The query keeps the original endpoint labels for ad hoc filters.

Arc length shows the total for each service or level. The `error` and `warn` overrides use edge display names from `legendFormat`. Link color comes from the target node.

panels.title: The lines behind the counts
panels.description:
These are the log lines that the relations charts count. Use them to compare a chart value with the source logs.

A derived field links a log line to Tempo when the line contains a `traceID` value.
